speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah
text: asked the Minister for Social and Family Development and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs in respect of youths getting radicalised online (a) how is MUIS utilising its digital platforms to combat this; (b) what is the level of reach and engagement of MUIS' SalamSG TV and MuslimSG to the general public and youths respectively; and (d) whether MUIS will consider supporting mysafespace.sg which connects users to certified asatizahs under the Asatizah Recognition Scheme for personalised and anonymous religious guidance through a chat portal.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: This includes disseminating positive and religiously accurate and context-appropriate narratives that inoculate Muslim youths in Singapore against inappropriate, divisive and exclusivist religious content.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: SalamSG TV and MuslimSG have achieved substantial reach and engagement, including with the youths.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: A significant portion of this reach is to youths.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Parents and families play an important role to inculcate the right values and understanding of our religion.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Sites like SalamSG and mysafespace.sg are good resources.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: But we should not, as parents, delegate our responsibility nor concede our duty of care to our children.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: In the meantime, MUIS will continue to support the development of our asatizah, so that they may provide religious guidance to the community, including reaching out through different and innovative ways, such as mysafespace.sg.

speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah (Nominated Member)
text: Is there a smaller breakdown available for the reach of these platforms?

speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah (Nominated Member)
text: And if not, will the Ministry consider collecting such data?

speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah (Nominated Member)
text: Because what we have right now is just for those aged 13 and 44.

speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah (Nominated Member)
text: It is even beyond the youth age range.

speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah (Nominated Member)
text: I am particularly heartened by it, because youths at that age do not really like to call the MUIS hotline.

speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah (Nominated Member)
text: They prefer to chat, they prefer to type.

speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah (Nominated Member)
text: It gives them an element of anonymity and a bit more confidence.

speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah (Nominated Member)
text: I was wondering, if there is any other way that MUIS or the Ministry would want to support them either to promote or even to help out with their website?

speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah (Nominated Member)
text: Because, right now, sometimes, it gets a bit buggy.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: On the first question, MUIS uses a particular service which gives this breakdown of their data.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: At this point of time, this service does not give very micro data that we can further analyse and see how we can understand the data.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Right now, we are looking at a broad reach and I think it is generally okay.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Unless there are necessary imperatives to spend more to get an even deeper dive, I think we will do with this for now.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: For the second question, I accept that the young people may not always want to go to MUIS' website.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: It is quite frightening sometimes to talk to an ustaz; or to be known talking to an ustaz; or find out that the ustaz even knows him.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: But the irony is that, if we endorse a particular site, which is actually a very independent and ground-up initiative, then we should also be mindful that youths think this is a MUIS site.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: And then, again, we lose the segment that this site, like mysafespace.sg, has gotten some reach to our youths.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: And therefore, endorsement is not something we should be doing just automatically.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: If useful, MUIS can put that in its SalamSG, for example, to say these are other independent sites that youths could reach out to if they want support.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: And if there is any need for our asatizah in that space for further support, they should reach out to MUIS and we would be happy to let them thrive and support them.
